body:
WHAT
NDJSON is 'one JSON object per line'. The decoder splits an incoming byte stream into lines and parses each. A line that is not valid JSON becomes an `{type:'error', fatal:false}` frame instead of throwing, blank lines are skipped, a trailing `\r` (CRLF) is removed, and a final line with no newline is still parsed when the stream ends.

WHY
One bad frame from either side must not take the whole session down with it.

WHERE
engine/protocol/src/ndjson.ts — `decodeFrames()` (async generator; CRLF strip via `.replace(/\r$/, '')`, trailing-buffer flush after the loop), `parseLine()` (catch → error frame), `encodeFrame()`.

TEST CHECKLIST
1. Feed chunks ['{"type":"a"}\nnot json\n{"type":"b"}\n']; decodeFrames yields three frames: {type:'a'}, an object with type 'error', fatal false and message starting 'unparseable frame:', then {type:'b'}.
2. Feed '{"type":"a"}\r\n' and assert the yielded frame equals {type:'a'} with no stray carriage return anywhere.
3. Feed a stream whose last chunk is '{"type":"tail"}' with no newline; after the stream ends the generator yields {type:'tail'}.
4. Feed one frame split across chunk boundaries ('{"ty', 'pe":"x"}\n') and assert exactly one frame {type:'x'} is yielded.
5. Feed '\n\n \n' and assert nothing is yielded (blank lines skipped, no error frames); the unparseable-frame message is truncated to at most 200 characters of the bad line.
